question.prompt: If \[ \frac{y}{x-z}=\frac{x+y}{z}=\frac{x}{y} \] for three positive numbers \(x,\) \(y,\) and \(z,\) all different, then \(\frac{x}{y}=\)

solutions.explanation:
Compare each of the first two fractions with \(x/y\). All denominators are nonzero because the numbers are positive and \(x\ne z\). Cross-multiplication gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
y^2&=x^2-xz,\\
xy+y^2&=xz.
\end{aligned}
\]
Adding these equations eliminates \(xz\), leaving
\[x^2-xy-2y^2=0.\]
Factoring now separates the possible ratios:
\[(x-2y)(x+y)=0.\]
Since \(x+y>0\), we must have \(x=2y\).

The second cross-multiplied equation then gives \(z=3y/2\). For every \(y>0\), these values satisfy \(x>z>y>0\), and substitution makes all three original ratios equal to \(2\). Hence the required ratio is \(\boxed{2}\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
solutions.title: Eliminate the shared product
